note: Hebrew tachash is uncertain (dugong/sea-cow, a dyed leather, or a fine leather from an Egyptian loanword); badgers are unlikely. Recurs in 4:8-14, 4:25. Context: a fine leather (medium confidence). As Exod 39:34.

mine: the jugs for the drink offering
note: Hebrew qesot hannesek are pitchers or jars "of the libation", vessels for pouring, not lids.
Hebrew mot is a pole-frame or litter for carrying, not a single bar.
Hebrew minchat hatamid is the continual grain offering; "meat" meant food in 1611 and now misleads.

kjv: to see when the holy things are covered
mine: to look at the holy things even for a moment
note: Hebrew kevalla' is literally "as a swallowing", most likely an idiom for "an instant" (like "a gulp"); the KJV took it as the covering ("swallowing up") of the objects. Context: even for a moment (medium confidence). 4:15-19 forbid the Kohathites to touch or see the holy things on pain of death; 'as a swallowing' is an idiom for an instant.
